subject: Business
title: Disruption from Below: The Low-End Attack
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Disruption from Below: The Low-End Attack.

hook.text: Southwest Airlines offered no meals, no assigned seats, and no frills. Airlines laughed.

buildup.text: Low-end disruption targets overserved customers who don't need all the features incumbents offer.

discovery.text: Disruptors strip away features to offer a simpler, cheaper product that's 'good enough' for most customers.

twist.text: Incumbents gladly shed low-profit customers. They don't realize that those customers were the majority of the market.

climax.text: Mini steel mills disrupted US Steel. They started with rebar (low-margin) and climbed to structural steel (high-margin).

punchline.text: The products people laugh at today dominate tomorrow.

quiz.question: How does low-end disruption typically begin?
options: By offering a simpler, cheaper product to overserved customers
By creating the most advanced product possible
By copying the incumbent's strategy exactly

details.summary: Low-end disruption targets overserved customers with simpler, cheaper products that established companies dismiss as inferior. Disruptors improve over time until the good-enough product satisfies mainstream customers, undermining incumbents who focused on premium features.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding low-end disruption explains why market leaders repeatedly lose to inferior newcomers. Companies focused on their best customers systematically ignore threats from below until it is too late to respond.
takeaways: Disruptors enter with cheaper, simpler products targeting overserved customers
Incumbents ignore low-end entrants because margins are unattractive initially
The disruptor improves until it satisfies mainstream needs at lower cost

faq.question: How did low-end disruption play out with personal computers?
faq.answer: Mainframe makers dismissed cheap PCs as toys for hobbyists. Mini-computer makers ignored them for the same reason. PCs improved rapidly until they could handle business tasks that previously required expensive systems. Each incumbents' profitable customer base was eventually captured.

faq.question: How can established companies defend against low-end disruption?
faq.answer: Create separate units with independent business models targeting the low end before disruptors do. Acquire potential disruptors early. Accept lower margins in new units. The hardest part is that defending against disruption requires cannibalizing your own profitable business.
